delivery_evidence_catalog.why_now: The survey note is the human-readable review anchor for the shipped starter packet and the remaining shared runtime-substrate blocker.
The module-slice note keeps the starter sample, loader scaffold, and bounded tests reviewable in one Phase 9 kretprobe packet.
The dedicated survey gate fails closed when the manifest, note, loader scaffold, or focused Phase 9 kretprobe build-step boundary drifts.
The focused `phase9-runtime-kretprobe-tests` step inside the shared Phase 9 build bundle keeps the kretprobe packet wired without claiming shared-loader ownership.

ownership_map.boundary: Records the shipped starter packet, points reviewers at the shared loader split, and keeps the remaining shared runtime-substrate blocker explicit.
Tracks the bounded starter sample, loader scaffold, and directly coupled tests without widening into shared runtime-loader ownership or runtime implementation.
Owns the in-memory runtime kretprobe starter and selftest hook without claiming live runtime-substrate parity.

Owns the sample-side loader-handoff scaffold, the idle registration snapshot, the loader-owned prepared and post-release metadata snapshot, and failed-exit retention checks, while the shared runtime-loader lane owns the reusable facade, contract, and allocator replay surfaces it consumes.
Fail-closes when the kretprobe manifest, survey note, loader scaffold, or focused Phase 9 kretprobe build-step boundary drifts.

Owns only the `phase9-runtime-kretprobe-tests` step in the shared Phase 9 replay bundle while the separate shared loader lane keeps the facade, contract, allocator/init-flow replay, and `phase9-runtime-loader-shared-tests` step aligned.

gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 9 build step is the narrowest honest place to widen runtime pilot coverage into the missing kretprobe lane.
A survey gate keeps the Linux anchor, landed starter status, and remaining runtime-substrate blocker explicit while the pilot stays small.

A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing kretprobe step that can model entry timestamps, return values, duration, missed-instance bookkeeping, and maxactive-pressure failed-exit recovery without claiming loadable-module parity.

A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter reviewable and bounded around lifecycle transitions, symbol retargeting, return-probe bookkeeping, and failed-exit state retention until the active probe drains.
The next meaningful step is a tiny table-driven gate that replays a few entry-skip, duration, and nmissed expectations from the Linux sample before widening the starter.

A bounded loader handoff keeps the planned register_kretprobe and unregister_kretprobe lifecycle, entry or exit symbol naming, private-data size, idle registration snapshot, prepared-snapshot ownership, post-release snapshot ownership, failed-exit state retention, prepared shared-request selftest-hook and runtime-substrate drift checks, and shared release-failure guards explicit while the real runtime substrate is still unavailable.

The shared runtime-loader contract keeps the bounded register_kretprobe and unregister_kretprobe handoff, allocator ownership, and request-shape limits explicit so the kretprobe starter does not overclaim runtime substrate parity.

The shared allocator and init-flow replay keeps the contract-backed request preparation, prepared-snapshot stability, and allocator handoff reviewable beside the kretprobe loader scaffold while the real runtime substrate remains blocked.

The roadmap's loadable runtime pilot module step still depends on a shared runtime substrate that can turn the bounded register_kretprobe and unregister_kretprobe handoff plan into a real loadable module path.
